title: Ferrari Purosangue vs Rolls-Royce Cullinan: The Real Difference

scenes.text: One is a Ferrari with four doors that asks you not to call it an SUV. The other is a Rolls-Royce named after a famous diamond. The Ferrari Purosangue and the Rolls-Royce Cullinan cost about the same, but on paper they are almost opposites. This is the real difference between them, and the places where our sources do not agree.
scenes.caption: FERRARI PUROSANGUE vs ROLLS-ROYCE CULLINAN: THE REAL DIFFERENCE

scenes.text: We read Wikipedia for both cars, Motor1, The Drive, Autoblog, Cars dot com, Robb Report, Carscoops and AOL. Ferrari's and Rolls-Royce's performance figures are the companies' own claims. Prices differ from source to source and year to year, so we show them all. And our own arithmetic is always labelled as ours.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: WIKIPEDIA · MOTOR1 · THE DRIVE · AUTOBLOG · CARS.COM · ROBB REPORT · CARSCOOPS · AOL · COMPANY FIGURES ARE CLAIMS · OUR ARITHMETIC IS LABELLED

scenes.text: Rolls-Royce got there first. Wikipedia says that at the Frankfurt show in twenty fifteen, chief executive Torsten Müller-Ötvös said the SUV would be revealed in twenty eighteen and sold in twenty nineteen. Testing reportedly began in January twenty sixteen. The name Cullinan was confirmed on the thirteenth of February twenty eighteen.
scenes.caption: 2015: TORSTEN MÜLLER-ÖTVÖS: REVEAL 2018, SALE 2019 · TESTING REPORTEDLY FROM 2 JAN 2016 · NAME CONFIRMED 13 FEB 2018 (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: The Cullinan was unveiled in May twenty eighteen at the Concorso d'Eleganza Villa d'Este in Italy, with a global launch in autumn that year in Jackson Hole, Wyoming. Wikipedia says that in twenty nineteen demand from established buyers exceeded supply, despite higher production and more hiring. The Series II production was announced in August twenty twenty-four.
scenes.caption: UNVEILED MAY 2018, VILLA D'ESTE · LAUNCH AUTUMN 2018, JACKSON HOLE · 2019 DEMAND EXCEEDED SUPPLY · SERIES II PRODUCTION ANNOUNCED AUG 2024 (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Ferrari's road was later and quieter. The car's code, F one seventy-five, started in twenty seventeen, and the reveal was on the thirteenth of September twenty twenty-two. By our arithmetic, the Cullinan was unveiled four years and four months before the Purosangue. Ferrari's chief executive Vigna asked that it not be called an SUV, because it is a Ferrari.
scenes.caption: CULLINAN MAY 2018 → PUROSANGUE 13 SEPT 2022 ≈ 4 YR 4 MO (OUR ARITHMETIC) · VIGNA: 'PLEASE DON'T CALL IT AN SUV' (AUTOEVOLUTION) · CODE F175, START 2017 (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Both firms say demand is high. Ferrari closed the Purosangue's order book before delivering one car, with a waiting list of about two years, and caps it at twenty percent of output. Rolls-Royce said in twenty nineteen that demand from established buyers exceeded supply. Neither source gives a unit count for either car.
scenes.caption: FERRARI: ORDER BOOK CLOSED, ~2-YEAR WAIT, 20% CAP (ROBB REPORT; CARSCOOPS) · ROLLS-ROYCE 2019: DEMAND EXCEEDED SUPPLY (WIKIPEDIA) · UNIT COUNTS FOR EITHER: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Wikipedia calls the Cullinan the second best-selling Rolls-Royce of all time, after the Silver Shadow, though it gives no sales figures. The Drive quotes the Rolls-Royce average buyer age as forty-two. We found no equivalent figure for Ferrari, so the two companies' customers are not compared in this video.
scenes.caption: CULLINAN = 2ND BEST-SELLING ROLLS-ROYCE EVER, AFTER SILVER SHADOW; NO UNIT FIGURES (WIKIPEDIA) · AVERAGE ROLLS-ROYCE BUYER AGE 42 (THE DRIVE) · FERRARI EQUIVALENT: NOT FOUND

scenes.text: Start with the Ferrari. Wikipedia lists a six point five litre naturally aspirated V12 making seven hundred fifteen horsepower at seventy-seven fifty rpm and five hundred twenty-eight pound-feet at sixty-two fifty. The Rolls-Royce has a six point seven five litre twin-turbo V12 making five hundred sixty-three horsepower at five thousand rpm and six hundred twenty-seven pound-feet at sixteen hundred.
scenes.caption: FERRARI 6.5 L NA V12: 715 HP @ 7,750 · 528 LB-FT @ 6,250 · ROLLS-ROYCE 6.75 L TWIN-TURBO V12: 563 HP @ 5,000 · 627 LB-FT @ 1,600 (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the Ferrari makes one hundred fifty-two more horsepower, which is twenty-seven percent more than the Rolls-Royce. The Rolls makes ninety-nine more pound-feet, nineteen percent more than the Ferrari. And it reaches its peak torque at sixteen hundred rpm, where the Ferrari is turning only at about a quarter of its redline.
scenes.caption: 715 − 563 = +152 HP (+27.0%) · 627 − 528 = +99 LB-FT (+18.8% FOR ROLLS) (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Black Badge version of the Cullinan makes six hundred horsepower in metric units, five hundred ninety-one in the American measure, and nine hundred newton-metres, or six hundred sixty-four pound-feet. Autoblog lists five hundred ninety-two horsepower. By our arithmetic, even the Black Badge gives away about one hundred twenty-three horsepower to the Ferrari.
scenes.caption: BLACK BADGE: 600 PS / 591 HP (WIKIPEDIA); 592 HP (AUTOBLOG) · 664 LB-FT · 715 − 592 = 123 HP BEHIND THE FERRARI (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Specific output makes the contrast. The Ferrari makes about one hundred ten horsepower a litre with no turbochargers. The Rolls-Royce makes about eighty-three. By our arithmetic, that is thirty-two percent more per litre for the Ferrari. The Rolls-Royce gets its strength at low revs from boost. The Ferrari asks you to rev it to the eighty-two fifty redline.
scenes.caption: 715 ÷ 6.5 ≈ 110.0 · 563 ÷ 6.75 ≈ 83.4 HP/L → +31.9% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · REDLINE 8,250 RPM (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Both use eight-speed automatic gearboxes and all-wheel drive. The Ferrari's is a dual-clutch unit from Magna, according to Wikipedia. The Rolls-Royce's is a ZF eight-speed automatic, the only option, with permanent all-wheel drive. Motor1 says the Ferrari's V12 peaks late, so you must rev it to build speed, which it calls more engaging.
scenes.caption: FERRARI: MAGNA 8DCL900 8-SPEED DCT, AWD · ROLLS-ROYCE: ZF 8HP 8-SPEED AUTOMATIC (ONLY OPTION), PERMANENT AWD (WIKIPEDIA) · MOTOR1: 'MORE ENGAGING' = REVIEWER'S VIEW

scenes.text: The sizes. The Purosangue is four thousand, nine hundred seventy-three millimetres long, two thousand, twenty-eight wide, fifteen eighty-nine high, with a three thousand, eighteen millimetre wheelbase. The Cullinan is five thousand, three hundred forty-one long, two thousand wide, eighteen thirty-five high, with a wheelbase of three thousand, two hundred ninety-five. These are Wikipedia's figures.
scenes.caption: FERRARI L 4,973 · W 2,028 · H 1,589 · WB 3,018 MM · ROLLS-ROYCE L 5,341 · W 2,000 · H 1,835 · WB 3,295 MM (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the Rolls is three hundred sixty-eight millimetres longer, seven percent, and two hundred forty-six millimetres taller, fifteen and a half percent. Its wheelbase is two hundred seventy-seven millimetres longer, nine percent. But the Ferrari is twenty-eight millimetres wider. A Ferrari that is wider than a Rolls-Royce is one of the surprises on this list.
scenes.caption: LENGTH +368 MM (+7.4%) · HEIGHT +246 MM (+15.5%) · WHEELBASE +277 MM (+9.2%) · WIDTH −28 MM (FERRARI WIDER, +1.4%) (OUR ARITHMETIC FROM WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Weight is the big difference. Wikipedia gives the Purosangue a kerb weight of two thousand, one hundred seventy kilograms and the Cullinan two thousand, six hundred sixty. By our arithmetic, the Rolls is four hundred ninety kilograms heavier, twenty-three percent more. Other sources give the Cullinan sixty-one eighty-five pounds, The Drive, or sixty-one seventy-three, Autoblog and Cars dot com.
scenes.caption: KERB: FERRARI 2,170 KG (4,784 LB) · ROLLS 2,660 KG (5,864 LB) (WIKIPEDIA) · ROLLS 6,085 LB (THE DRIVE) · 6,173 LB (AUTOBLOG; CARS.COM) · +490 KG = +22.6% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Using the heaviest figures, the Rolls-Royce is one thousand, three hundred eighty-nine pounds heavier than the Ferrari's four thousand, seven hundred eighty-four. By our arithmetic, that is twenty-nine percent more. It is the weight of a small car. Autoblog says the Cullinan's weight limits its agility, and Motor1 says the Ferrari handles like a sports sedan.
scenes.caption: 6,173 − 4,784 = 1,389 LB = +29.0% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · AUTOBLOG: WEIGHT 'LIMITS AGILITY' (ROLLS) · MOTOR1: FERRARI 'LIKE A SPORTS SEDAN'

scenes.text: Power per weight, by our arithmetic. The Ferrari has about three hundred thirty horsepower per tonne. The Rolls-Royce, on Wikipedia's weight, has about two hundred twelve. That means the Ferrari has fifty-six percent more power for each tonne it carries. Pounds per horsepower, the Ferrari is six point seven, and the Rolls ten point four.
scenes.caption: 715 ÷ 2.170 = 329.5 · 563 ÷ 2.660 = 211.7 HP/TONNE → +55.7% · 4,784 ÷ 715 = 6.7 · 5,864 ÷ 563 = 10.4 LB/HP (OUR ARITHMETIC; WIKIPEDIA WEIGHTS)

scenes.text: Speed claims. Ferrari claims zero to one hundred kilometres per hour in three point three seconds, zero to two hundred in ten point six, and a top speed over three hundred ten. Autoblog lists the Cullinan at five seconds flat to sixty, or four point nine for the Black Badge. Wikipedia gives its top speed as two hundred fifty, limited.
scenes.caption: FERRARI: 0–100 3.3 S · 0–200 10.6 S · >310 KM/H (CLAIMS) · ROLLS: 0–60 5.0 S (4.9 BLACK BADGE) (AUTOBLOG) · TOP SPEED 250 KM/H (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, one point seven seconds separates the claims, though Ferrari's is to one hundred kilometres per hour and Rolls-Royce's to sixty miles per hour. Sixty miles per hour is slightly slower, about ninety-seven kilometres per hour, so the real gap is a little larger. And the Ferrari's top speed is sixty kilometres per hour higher, twenty-four percent.
scenes.caption: 5.0 − 3.3 = 1.7 S (DIFFERENT SPEED TARGETS: 100 KM/H vs 60 MPH ≈ 96.6 KM/H) · 310 − 250 = +60 KM/H = +24% (OUR ARITHMETIC; CLAIMS)

scenes.text: Motor1 estimated the Purosangue's zero to sixty at three point two seconds, labelled as an estimate, not measured. Its spec sheet lists a top speed of one hundred ninety-two miles per hour. We found no independent measured acceleration for either car, and no track comparison. So the speed gap is a gap between claims.
scenes.caption: MOTOR1: 0–60 3.2 S ESTIMATED; TOP 192 MPH (SPEC SHEET) · INDEPENDENT MEASURED TIMES, EITHER CAR: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The Drive's Jerry Perez, reviewing the Cullinan Series II on Pikes Peak Highway in July twenty twenty-five, wrote: If I told you this seventeen and a half foot long SUV cornered like a sports car, I'd be lying. He praised its tyre grip and four-wheel steering, and said the steering is calibrated for smooth driving rather than quick reflexes.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE (JERRY PEREZ, 10 JULY 2025): 'IF I TOLD YOU THIS 17.5-FOOT-LONG SUV CORNERED LIKE A SPORTS CAR, I'D BE LYING' · PRAISED GRIP, 4-WHEEL STEERING · STEERING CALIBRATED FOR SMOOTHNESS

scenes.text: The Ferrari's suspension, from Motor1, uses Multimatic active dampers with electric motors, independent left and right, with no sway bars. The Rolls-Royce, from Wikipedia, has a double-wishbone front and five-link rear, self-levelling air suspension, electronically controlled dampers, and electrically actuated active anti-roll bars. Both are active systems, built for opposite aims.
scenes.caption: FERRARI: MULTIMATIC ACTIVE DAMPERS (ELECTRIC MOTORS), INDEPENDENT SIDES, NO SWAY BARS (MOTOR1) · ROLLS: DOUBLE-WISHBONE / 5-LINK, AIR SUSPENSION, ELECTRONIC DAMPERS, ACTIVE ANTI-ROLL BARS (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: The Rolls-Royce also has a Flagbearer stereo camera that scans the road ahead and adjusts the suspension, working up to one hundred kilometres per hour, and four-wheel steering as on the Phantom. Its off-road mode raises the ride height by forty millimetres. Motor1 says the Purosangue has no off-road capability. The Drive's drive route was paved.
scenes.caption: ROLLS: 'FLAGBEARER' STEREO CAMERA TO 100 KM/H · 4-WHEEL STEERING · OFF-ROAD MODE +40 MM (WIKIPEDIA) · FERRARI: 'NO OFF-ROAD CAPABILITY' (MOTOR1) · THE DRIVE'S ROUTE: PAVED (PIKES PEAK HIGHWAY)

scenes.text: The platforms. Wikipedia says the Cullinan sits on Rolls-Royce's aluminium spaceframe, the Architecture of Luxury, which debuted on the Phantom. The Purosangue, it says, shares a platform with the Ferrari Roma. One began as a larger car's structure, and the other as a coupe's. That is Wikipedia's account, and neither company explains it further.
scenes.caption: ROLLS: ALUMINIUM SPACEFRAME 'ARCHITECTURE OF LUXURY' (DEBUTED ON PHANTOM VIII) · FERRARI: SHARES PLATFORM WITH ROMA (WIKIPEDIA) · NEITHER COMPANY'S EXPLANATION IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Seating. The Ferrari has four seats, with two individual seats in the back and no rear bench option, according to Motor1. The Rolls-Royce offers four or five seats, with a lounge or individual layout, though Cars dot com's page lists both four and five. Wikipedia also mentions two-or-three-across rear seating, a glass partition, and cocktail-suite seats in the boot.
scenes.caption: FERRARI: 4 SEATS, NO REAR BENCH OPTION (MOTOR1) · ROLLS: 4 OR 5 SEATS (AUTOBLOG; CARS.COM LISTS BOTH) · OPTIONS: GLASS PARTITION, 'COCKTAIL SUITE' BOOT SEATS (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Cargo space, from Cars dot com: seventeen cubic feet behind the first row of the Ferrari, nine behind the second, and twenty-one cubic feet for the Rolls-Royce. By our arithmetic, the Rolls has twenty-four percent more space with the rear seats folded, and more than double the Ferrari's with the rear seats in use. Motor1 calls the Ferrari's trunk real, and says it held luggage for a road trip.
scenes.caption: CARS.COM: FERRARI 17 CU FT (TO SEAT 1) / 9 (TO SEAT 2) · ROLLS 21 / 21 · 21 vs 17 = +23.5% (SEATS FOLDED) · 21 vs 9 = +133% (REAR SEATS IN USE) (OUR ARITHMETIC) · MOTOR1: 'REAL TRUNK'

scenes.text: Technology. The Rolls-Royce Series II has a digital gauge cluster and the new Spirit infotainment system, which The Drive found fairly intuitive after three days, but Autoblog says trails newer BMW systems. The Ferrari has two front displays, and Motor1 criticises its touch-capacitive controls, and a cluster that loses the tachometer when CarPlay is on.
scenes.caption: ROLLS SERIES II: DIGITAL CLUSTER + 'SPIRIT' SYSTEM — THE DRIVE: 'FAIRLY INTUITIVE'; AUTOBLOG: TRAILS NEWER BMW SYSTEMS · FERRARI: TWO FRONT DISPLAYS; TOUCH-CAPACITIVE CONTROLS CRITICISED; NO TACHOMETER WITH CARPLAY (MOTOR1)

scenes.text: At launch, Wikipedia says some critics noted that the Cullinan lacked automatic climate control and partially autonomous cruise control, found on less expensive SUVs. We do not know whether those gaps were fixed in the Series II. The Drive praised the interior craftsmanship as one of the most intricate it had seen on any vehicle.
scenes.caption: LAUNCH CRITICISM: NO AUTOMATIC CLIMATE CONTROL / PARTIALLY AUTONOMOUS CRUISE (WIKIPEDIA) · SERIES II FIXES: NOT STATED · THE DRIVE: INTERIOR CRAFTSMANSHIP 'ONE OF THE MOST INTRICATE'

scenes.text: Now the price, which is not as simple as it looks. For twenty twenty-five, The Drive lists the Cullinan Series II at four hundred five thousand dollars, and Motor1 lists the Purosangue at four hundred twenty-three thousand, six hundred eighty-six. By our arithmetic, the Rolls-Royce is eighteen thousand, six hundred eighty-six dollars cheaper, four point four percent.
scenes.caption: CULLINAN SERIES II $405,000 (THE DRIVE) vs PUROSANGUE $423,686 (MOTOR1) → ROLLS $18,686 CHEAPER = 4.4% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: For twenty twenty-six, Autoblog lists the Cullinan Series II at four hundred thirty-two thousand, three hundred fifty, and Cars dot com lists the Purosangue at four hundred twenty-three thousand, six hundred thirty-six. Now the Ferrari is eight thousand, seven hundred fourteen dollars cheaper, two percent. The ordering has flipped, though the sources and years differ.
scenes.caption: CULLINAN SERIES II $432,350 (AUTOBLOG) vs PUROSANGUE $423,636 (CARS.COM) → FERRARI $8,714 CHEAPER = 2.1% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: For twenty twenty-seven, Cars dot com lists the Cullinan at four hundred twenty-nine thousand, six hundred and the Purosangue still at four hundred twenty-three thousand, six hundred thirty-six. Autoblog's twenty twenty-seven page says four hundred thirty-five thousand, nine hundred fifty. Three Cullinan prices from three pages, spanning six thousand, three hundred fifty dollars.
scenes.caption: CULLINAN 2027: $429,600 (CARS.COM) vs $435,950 (AUTOBLOG) → $6,350 APART · PUROSANGUE $423,636 (CARS.COM) (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: And how far have they come? Wikipedia gives the Cullinan's launch price as approximately three hundred twenty-five thousand dollars. By our arithmetic, Autoblog's four hundred thirty-five thousand, nine hundred fifty is a hundred ten thousand, nine hundred fifty more, or thirty-four percent. The Ferrari had its first US price at three hundred ninety-eight thousand, three hundred fifty in twenty twenty-four.
scenes.caption: CULLINAN LAUNCH ~$325,000 → $435,950 (2027) = +$110,950 = +34.1% (WIKIPEDIA; AUTOBLOG; OUR ARITHMETIC) · PUROSANGUE FIRST US PRICE $398,350 (AOL) → $423,636 (2026) = +6.3%

scenes.text: Black Badge pricing: Autoblog lists the twenty twenty-six Black Badge Cullinan Series II at five hundred two thousand, three hundred fifty and the twenty twenty-seven at five hundred four thousand, nine hundred fifty. By our arithmetic, that is sixty-nine thousand dollars more than the standard Cullinan of twenty twenty-seven. The Ferrari has no sibling trim in our sources.
scenes.caption: BLACK BADGE: $502,350 (2026) · $504,950 (2027) vs STANDARD $435,950 → +$69,000 (+15.8%) (AUTOBLOG; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Put the starting prices in context with the Census Bureau's median household income of eighty-three thousand, seven hundred thirty dollars. By our arithmetic, four hundred twenty-three thousand, six hundred thirty-six is five years of it, and four hundred thirty-five thousand, nine hundred fifty is five point two years. Both are about eight and a half times the average new vehicle.
scenes.caption: $423,636 ÷ $83,730 = 5.06 YR · $435,950 ÷ $83,730 = 5.21 YR · ÷ $50,089 AVG NEW = 8.5× / 8.7× (CENSUS; KBB; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Options. The Drive's Cullinan cost five hundred seventy-two thousand, five hundred fifty dollars as tested, against four hundred five thousand base. By our arithmetic, that is one hundred sixty-seven thousand, five hundred fifty in options, forty-one percent. Three items are priced: the Duality Twill interior at seventeen thousand, the Twilight Purple paint at thirteen thousand, the Shooting Star Headliner at nine thousand.
scenes.caption: $572,550 AS TESTED − $405,000 BASE = $167,550 = +41.4% · INTERIOR $17,000 + PAINT $13,000 + HEADLINER $9,000 = $39,000 FOR THREE ITEMS (THE DRIVE; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Motor1's Ferrari reached five hundred six thousand, three hundred five dollars as tested, which is eighty-two thousand, six hundred nineteen above its base, nineteen and a half percent. Rolls-Royce's president for North America, Colbeth, said, in The Drive: We are not here to judge the customer, but guide them through the creation process. Options are a big part of both brands.
scenes.caption: FERRARI $506,305 − $423,686 = $82,619 = +19.5% · ROLLS-ROYCE NA PRESIDENT COLBETH: 'WE ARE NOT HERE TO JUDGE THE CUSTOMER, BUT GUIDE THEM THROUGH THE CREATION PROCESS' (MOTOR1; THE DRIVE; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Fuel economy. Autoblog and Cars dot com give the Cullinan twelve city, nineteen highway and fourteen combined. Autoblog's twenty twenty-seven page says eleven, eighteen and thirteen. The Ferrari is eleven, fifteen and twelve. By our arithmetic, at fifteen thousand miles a year, the Ferrari burns about one hundred seventy-nine gallons more than a Rolls rated at fourteen.
scenes.caption: FERRARI 11/15/12 · ROLLS 12/19/14 (2026) OR 11/18/13 (2027, AUTOBLOG) · 15,000 MI: 1,250 GAL vs 1,071 GAL → +179 GAL (OUR ARITHMETIC; MILEAGE ASSUMED)

scenes.text: At four dollars, twenty-eight cents a gallon for regular, from the Energy Information Administration, that is about seven hundred sixty-five dollars a year. Autoblog says the Rolls needs premium gasoline, and our sources have no premium price or Ferrari fuel grade, so the real figure may be higher. Fuel is small beside the purchase price of either car.
scenes.caption: 179 GAL × $4.284 ≈ $765/YEAR (REGULAR PRICE, EIA 19 OCT 2026; OUR ARITHMETIC) · ROLLS NEEDS PREMIUM (AUTOBLOG) · PREMIUM PRICE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Warranty. Autoblog lists the Rolls-Royce with a basic warranty, powertrain, roadside assistance and maintenance each for four years and unlimited miles, and corrosion for six. Cars dot com lists the Ferrari's basic warranty as three years. We have no source on the Ferrari's maintenance plan, so we cannot compare the cost of keeping each one serviced.
scenes.caption: ROLLS: 4 YR / UNLIMITED MI (BASIC, POWERTRAIN, ROADSIDE, MAINTENANCE) · 6 YR CORROSION (AUTOBLOG) · FERRARI: 3-YR BASIC (CARS.COM) · FERRARI MAINTENANCE PLAN: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Tax. AOL says the Purosangue's price excludes any gas guzzler tax because the government had not yet classified the car. Wikipedia says the Cullinan is not exempt, because it is classed as a station wagon. We did not find the final amount for either, so any difference in tax is not in our numbers.
scenes.caption: PUROSANGUE: PRICE EXCLUDES TAX, CLASSIFICATION PENDING (AOL) · CULLINAN: NOT EXEMPT (WIKIPEDIA) · AMOUNTS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Rarity is where the cars differ in the sources. Wikipedia says the Cullinan Blue Shadow, a Black Badge special edition inspired by the Kármán line, was limited to sixty-two cars. Autoblog's twenty twenty-seven page mentions a four-unit Cullinan Yachting and a five-unit Black Badge by Cyril Kongo. The Cullinan is a regular production car, but with tiny one-offs.
scenes.caption: BLUE SHADOW: 62 UNITS (WIKIPEDIA) · CULLINAN YACHTING: 4 UNITS · BLACK BADGE BY CYRIL KONGO: 5 UNITS (AUTOBLOG 2027) · ALL SMALL RUNS OF A REGULAR CAR

scenes.text: The Ferrari's rarity is a rule, not a trim. Robb Report, Carscoops and Motor1 all say it is capped at twenty percent of Ferrari's output. By our arithmetic, that is up to two thousand, seven hundred twenty-eight cars on thirteen thousand, six hundred forty deliveries in twenty twenty-five. The Cullinan's volume has no published cap in our sources.
scenes.caption: 20% × 13,640 (2025 DELIVERIES, AUTOHLED) = 2,728 MAX (OUR ARITHMETIC) · CULLINAN VOLUME CAP: NONE IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Awards. Wikipedia says the Purosangue won the Compasso d'Oro industrial design award in twenty twenty-four. Its Cullinan page lists no awards. The Drive's quick take on the Cullinan is: It's a whole lotta money, but it's a whole lotta car. Autoblog's verdict calls it the highest level of luxury SUV available.
scenes.caption: PUROSANGUE: COMPASSO D'ORO 2024 (WIKIPEDIA) · CULLINAN: NO AWARDS LISTED · THE DRIVE: 'A WHOLE LOTTA MONEY, BUT A WHOLE LOTTA CAR' · AUTOBLOG: 'HIGHEST LEVEL OF LUXURY SUV AVAILABLE'

scenes.text: A quick conversion for scale. By our arithmetic, five thousand, three hundred forty-one millimetres is seventeen and a half feet, which matches The Drive's phrase about a seventeen and a half foot long SUV. The Ferrari's four thousand, nine hundred seventy-three millimetres is sixteen point three feet. The Rolls is about fourteen inches longer, which is the Cars dot com figure too.
scenes.caption: 5,341 MM = 17.5 FT · 4,973 MM = 16.3 FT → +1.2 FT (≈ 14 IN) (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC; THE DRIVE: '17.5-FOOT-LONG')

scenes.text: Torque per tonne is almost a tie. By our arithmetic, the Ferrari delivers about two hundred forty-three pound-feet for each tonne of its weight, and the Rolls-Royce about two hundred thirty-six, a gap of just three percent. The Ferrari's advantage is all in horsepower, which depends on engine speed, and the Rolls-Royce's torque arrives at a quarter of the revs.
scenes.caption: 528 ÷ 2.170 ≈ 243 · 627 ÷ 2.660 ≈ 236 LB-FT/TONNE → FERRARI +3.2% (OUR ARITHMETIC; WIKIPEDIA WEIGHTS)

scenes.text: The Black Badge changes that little. At five hundred ninety-two horsepower and two thousand, six hundred sixty kilograms, by our arithmetic, it makes about two hundred twenty-three horsepower per tonne, against the Ferrari's three hundred thirty. Autoblog's review of the standard car says the Cullinan's appeal is luxury, comfort and customisation rather than speed.
scenes.caption: 592 ÷ 2.660 ≈ 222.6 vs 329.5 HP/TONNE (OUR ARITHMETIC) · AUTOBLOG: APPEAL = 'LUXURY, COMFORT AND CUSTOMIZATION RATHER THAN SPEED'

scenes.text: A lighter car that uses more fuel. The Ferrari is eighteen percent lighter than the Rolls-Royce but is rated twelve miles per gallon, against fourteen. By our arithmetic, that means the Ferrari uses about seventeen percent more fuel for every mile. The engine, not the weight, is what decides the fuel economy here, at least on the sources' own ratings.
scenes.caption: FERRARI 12 MPG vs ROLLS 14 MPG → (1/12) ÷ (1/14) = 1.167 → +16.7% FUEL PER MILE · 18.4% LIGHTER (OUR ARITHMETIC; EPA FIGURES VIA WIKIPEDIA/CARS.COM)

scenes.text: The Series II update, in twenty twenty-four, changed the look and the technology but not the powertrain. Wikipedia lists a new front bumper, new headlights, an illuminated grille, twenty-three-inch wheels, new interior materials, a digital gauge cluster and a new infotainment system. Autoblog's twenty twenty-seven page says the Cullinan remains unchanged apart from special series and one-off cars.
scenes.caption: SERIES II (2024): NEW BUMPER, HEADLIGHTS, ILLUMINATED GRILLE, 23-IN WHEELS, NEW INTERIOR MATERIALS, DIGITAL CLUSTER, NEW INFOTAINMENT · NO POWERTRAIN CHANGE (WIKIPEDIA) · 2027 'REMAINS UNCHANGED' (AUTOBLOG)

scenes.text: What The Drive disliked about the Cullinan: the steering is calibrated for smooth driving rather than quick reflexes, throttle and steering inputs take time to get used to on a vehicle this size, and the seat colour palette may not suit everyone. What it liked: the craftsmanship, four-wheel steering, self-levelling air suspension, and Pirelli P Zero grip that let it carry more speed than the reviewer was comfortable with.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE: DISLIKED — STEERING TUNED FOR SMOOTHNESS, TIME TO ADAPT TO SIZE, SEAT PALETTE · LIKED — CRAFTSMANSHIP, 4-WHEEL STEERING, AIR SUSPENSION, PIRELLI PZERO GRIP

scenes.text: The Cullinan's name, Wikipedia says, comes from the Cullinan diamond. The page describes that stone in two ways: as the largest gem-quality rough diamond ever discovered, and, elsewhere, as the largest diamond ever found, at three thousand one hundred carats. The page does not reconcile the two descriptions. The Ferrari's name, Wikipedia says, is that of a horse breed.
scenes.caption: CULLINAN = NAMED AFTER THE CULLINAN DIAMOND: 'LARGEST GEM-QUALITY ROUGH DIAMOND EVER DISCOVERED' vs 'LARGEST DIAMOND EVER FOUND AT 3100 CARATS' — WIKIPEDIA DOES NOT RECONCILE · PUROSANGUE = HORSE BREED

scenes.text: Both firms also sell the idea of a long wait. Ferrari's order book covered the entire twenty twenty-five production year, according to Motor1, with orders then going to twenty twenty-six. Rolls-Royce said in twenty nineteen that demand exceeded supply. Our sources do not say how long the wait for a Cullinan is today, or whether either wait still exists.
scenes.caption: FERRARI: ORDER BOOK COVERED ALL OF 2025; NEW ORDERS → 2026 (MOTOR1, Q3 2023) · ROLLS 2019: DEMAND > SUPPLY (WIKIPEDIA) · CURRENT WAITS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: What is missing. A test that put the two cars side by side. Independent measured acceleration for either. Unit sales for the Cullinan and the Purosangue. A like-for-like year price comparison from one source. Ferrari's maintenance costs. And a final gas guzzler tax for either car.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: SIDE-BY-SIDE TEST · MEASURED ACCELERATION · UNIT SALES · SAME-SOURCE PRICE COMPARISON · FERRARI MAINTENANCE COSTS · FINAL GAS GUZZLER TAX
scenes.chapter: What our sources do not say

scenes.text: So the real difference, on the paper we have, is this. The Ferrari has twenty-seven percent more power, a body eighteen percent lighter, and claimed speed to match, with an engine that wants revs. The Rolls-Royce has more torque at lower revs, more cargo space, a longer warranty, and a ride built around comfort. The price gap flips with the year.
scenes.caption: FERRARI: +27% POWER, −18.4% WEIGHT (vs ROLLS: 490 ÷ 2,660), CLAIMED FASTER · ROLLS: +19% TORQUE LOWER DOWN, +24% CARGO (SEATS FOLDED), 4-YR WARRANTY · PRICE ORDER FLIPS BY YEAR/SOURCE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Which would you take, the Ferrari or the Rolls-Royce? Tell us in the comments. In the other videos of this series, we reveal two things you did not know about the Purosangue, ask whether a normal person can afford one, and tell why Ferrari swore it would never build an SUV.
